llm.summary: This skill is purpose-aligned as a continuous-learning assistant, but it creates persistent jobs, exports stored memories to an external model API, and lets model output modify future agent-governing documents without enough user control.

dimensions.detail: For the stated goal, access to persistent memories and local documents is expected, but exporting the full matching diary history plus metadata to a third-party endpoint without redaction, preview, or per-transfer consent is overbroad.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer asks for confirmation before scheduling jobs, so persistence is disclosed, but it installs recurring cron or Scheduled Task execution for sync and dream analysis and lacks an uninstall path, expiration, or integrity checks. Unix cron commands interpolate unquoted workspace paths, and Windows subprocess calls use shell=True.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad activation language for new-task detection and directs agents to read and obey mutable profile, workflow, tool, and bootstrap documents. Remote model output can become durable instructions with only document-name validation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Daily background execution persists beyond the interactive session and can continue reading memory, writing notification queues, contacting the model API, and changing agent-governing files under the installing user's account.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose fits memory capture, scheduled analysis, and document updates, but the implementation reads all MemPalace diary entries and metadata, sends them to MiniMax-compatible API analysis, and appends returned content into SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, and BOOTSTRAP.md, which are used as future agent instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill if you are comfortable with persistent local memory, unattended daily jobs, and possible transfer of stored conversations and metadata to a configured model provider. Do not store secrets or regulated data in MemPalace with this enabled, and avoid installing the scheduler until there is explicit opt-in, redaction, review-before-write, and an uninstall path.
llm.findings:
[T02] unexpected: Confirmed in dream/dream_cycle.py: remote analysis results are parsed and appended into future agent-governing documents without semantic validation or review.
[T05] expected: External model analysis is consistent with the described dream-analysis feature, but the code exports all matching diary entries and metadata without minimization or consent controls.
[T06] expected: Scheduled execution is disclosed and related to the daily sync/dream workflow, but it is persistent and under-scoped for a skill installation because no uninstall, expiry, or integrity control is provided.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed implementation weaknesses include unquoted shell-interpreted cron commands, shell=True around Windows task commands, config/schema mismatch, and destructive reinitialization of learning files.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent conversation memory and later analysis are core features, but the artifacts do not provide a prominent privacy notice, retention rules, redaction, deletion controls, or clear external-transfer consent.
[SSD-3] expected: Long-term memory and profile documents are expected for this skill, but the schema is broad and consolidates user preferences, project background, decisions, tool notes, and bootstrap behavior into durable files.
[E1] expected: The MiniMax endpoint is documented, but the implementation sends diary contents and metadata to the remote API without preview, redaction, or a reliable documented configuration path.
[RA2] expected: Cron and Scheduled Tasks are expected for daily automation but materially amplify the privacy and memory-poisoning risks because they run unattended.
[YR1] expected: Downgraded: the matched text is troubleshooting guidance using crontab -l and grep, not a backdoor payload.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: setup/install_cron.py was present in the workspace and was inspected directly.
[TM1] unexpected: Confirmed unsafe subprocess parameterization in setup/install_cron.py; task scheduling is expected, but shell=True is not needed and increases execution risk.
[SQP-1] unexpected: New-task detection is vague enough to trigger memory reads and persistence during ordinary topic changes rather than explicit user-directed use.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill implies file I/O, shell scheduling, local memory database access, and network API calls, but it does not declare clear least-privilege boundaries or opt-in subcommands.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation appears consistent with the package audience and is not a security concern by itself.
